agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Texas statute prohibiting capture of biometric identifiers (retina or iris scans, fingerprints, voiceprints, hand or face geometry) for a commercial purpose without notice and consent. Also limits disclosure, requires reasonable-care storage and destruction, and imposes civil penalties up to $25,000 per violation. Originally effective April 1, 2009.
summary.long: Prohibits a person from capturing a biometric identifier (retina or iris scan, fingerprint, voiceprint, or record of hand or face geometry) for a commercial purpose unless the person first informs the individual and receives consent. Images found on the internet or other public sources do not count as notice or consent unless the individual made them public. A person possessing such an identifier may not sell, lease or otherwise disclose it, subject to listed exceptions (disappearance or death, financial transactions, federal or state statute, warrants), and must store and protect it with at least the care applied to other confidential information. Destruction is due within a reasonable time and no later than the first anniversary of the purpose expiring; the period extends where another law requires longer retention, and is presumed to expire on termination of employment for identifiers an employer collected for security. The Attorney General may sue for a civil penalty of up to $25,000 per violation. Exclusions cover voiceprints held by financial institutions, AI training, processing and storage (unless used to uniquely identify a person), and security or fraud purposes. Identifiers captured to train an AI system and later used commercially fall under the section's possession and destruction duties and penalties. Amended in 2009, 2017 and 2025 (2025 amendment effective January 1, 2026).

obligations.summary: A person may not capture a biometric identifier of an individual for a commercial purpose unless the person informs the individual and receives the individual's consent (Sec. 503.001(b)). Applies to retina or iris scans, fingerprints, voiceprints and hand or face geometry (Sec. 503.001(a)(2)). Sec. 503.001(b-1) states that publicly available images do not count as notice or consent unless the individual made them public.
